chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Urama, raising it from Mu'alla ibn Khunays, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the right of the believer, so he said: 'Seventy rights. I will not inform you of all of them, but only seven, for I am sympathetic towards you, fearing that you will not be able to bear them.' So I said, 'Yes, if Allah wills.'

He said: 'You should not be satiated while he is hungry, nor be clothed while he is bare; you should be his guide, his shirt which he wears, and his tongue which he speaks with; you should love for him what you love for yourself; and if you have a maid, you should send her to prepare his bed and attend to his needs by night and day. So when you do that, your Wilayah is linked with our Wilayah, and our Wilayah is linked with the Wilayah of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.'
ai.seo_question: What are the seven rights of a believer upon their brother according to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) condenses the seventy rights of a believer into seven core principles, emphasizing radical selflessness where one prioritizes the brother's comfort over one's own. The narration highlights practical manifestations of faith, such as sharing sustenance and clothing, acting as a guide, and even utilizing servants to serve the brother's needs, thereby transforming social relations into spiritual acts. This fulfillment of rights is theologically significant in Shia tradition as it establishes a chain of Wilayah, linking the believer's loyalty to the Imams and ultimately to Allah.
